items.informal_name: Linearity of Cramer's Rule over Finite Sums in Commutative Rings
items.type:
∀ {n : Type v} {α : Type w} [inst : DecidableEq n] [inst_1 : Fintype n] [inst_2 : CommRing α] (A : Matrix n n α)
  {β : Type u_1} (s : Finset β) (f : β → n → α), ∑ x ∈ s, A.cramer (f x) = A.cramer (∑ x ∈ s, f x)
items.informal_description: For a matrix $ A $ over a commutative ring $ \alpha $, a finite set $ s $, and a function $ f : \beta \to n \to \alpha $, the sum of the Cramer's rule determinants $ \sum_{x \in s} \text{cramer}(A, f(x)) $ equals the Cramer's rule determinant of the sum $ \text{cramer}\left(A, \sum_{x \in s} f(x)\right) $. This establishes that the Cramer's rule linear map preserves finite sums in the context of commutative rings.

items.informal_name: Determinant Invariance Under Row Addition Outside a Finite Set
items.type:
∀ {n : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq n] [inst_1 : Fintype n] {R : Type v} [inst_2 : CommRing R] {A B : Matrix n n R}
  {s : Finset n} (c : n → R), (∀ i ∉ s, c i = 0) → ∀ k ∉ s, (∀ (i j : n), A i j = B i j + c i * B k j) → A.det = B.det
items.informal_description: If two $ n \times n $ matrices $ A $ and $ B $ over a commutative ring $ R $ satisfy $ A_{i,j} = B_{i,j} + c_i B_{k,j} $ for all rows $ i \notin s $ (where $ s $ is a finite subset of rows and $ k \notin s $), and $ c_i = 0 $ for all $ i \in s $, then the determinants of $ A $ and $ B $ are equal, i.e., $ \det(A) = \det(B) $. This expresses that adding a scalar multiple of a fixed row $ k $ to other rows outside $ s $ does not change the determinant.

items.informal_name: Cramer's Rule Preserves Finite Sums in Commutative Rings
items.type:
∀ {n : Type v} {α : Type w} [inst : DecidableEq n] [inst_1 : Fintype n] [inst_2 : CommRing α] (A : Matrix n n α)
  {β : Type u_1} (s : Finset β) (f : n → β → α) (i : n),
  ∑ x ∈ s, A.cramer (fun j => f j x) i = A.cramer (fun j => ∑ x ∈ s, f j x) i
items.informal_description: For a matrix $ A $ over a commutative ring $ \alpha $, finite set $ s $, function $ f : n \to \beta \to \alpha $, and index $ i $, the sum over $ x \in s $ of the Cramer's rule solution $ \text{cramer}_A $ applied to the vector $ j \mapsto f(j, x) $ at index $ i $ equals $ \text{cramer}_A $ applied to the vector $ j \mapsto \sum_{x \in s} f(j, x) $ at index $ i $.

items.informal_name: Distributive Property of Multilinear Maps Over Finite Sums
items.type:
∀ {R : Type uR} {ι : Type uι} {M₁ : ι → Type v₁} {M₂ : Type v₂} [inst : Semiring R]
  [inst_1 : (i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (M₁ i)] [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid M₂] [inst_3 : (i : ι) → Module R (M₁ i)]
  [inst_4 : Module R M₂] (f : MultilinearMap R M₁ M₂) {α : ι → Type u_1} (g : (i : ι) → α i → M₁ i)
  (A : (i : ι) → Finset (α i)) [inst_5 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_6 : Fintype ι] {n : ℕ},
  ∑ i, (A i).card = n → (f fun i => ∑ j ∈ A i, g i j) = ∑ r ∈ Fintype.piFinset A, f fun i => g i (r i)
items.informal_description: For a multilinear map $ f $, the application of $ f $ to the sum of $ g(i, j) $ over each $ j \in A(i) $ is equal to the sum over all functions $ r $ in the product of $ A(i) $ of $ f $ applied to $ g(i, r(i)) $. Formally, $ f\left(\lambda i. \sum_{j \in A(i)} g(i, j)\right) = \sum_{r \in \prod_{i} A(i)} f\left(\lambda i. g(i, r(i))\right) $.

  [inst_1 : (i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (M₁ i)] [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid M₂] [inst_3 : (i : ι) → Module R (M₁ i)]
  [inst_4 : Module R M₂] (f : MultilinearMap R M₁ M₂) {α : ι → Type u_1} (g : (i : ι) → α i → M₁ i)
  (A : (i : ι) → Finset (α i)) [inst_5 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_6 : Fintype ι],
  (f fun i => ∑ j ∈ A i, g i j) = ∑ r ∈ Fintype.piFinset A, f fun i => g i (r i)
items.informal_description: For a multilinear map $ f $ and a family of finite sets $ A_i $ indexed by a finite type $ \iota $ with decidable equality, the application of $ f $ to the function $ i \mapsto \sum_{j \in A_i} g(i,j) $ equals the sum over all functions $ r $ in the product $ \prod_{i \in \iota} A_i $ of $ f $ applied to the function $ i \mapsto g(i, r(i)) $. In symbols: $ f\left(\lambda i. \sum_{j \in A_i} g(i,j)\right) = \sum_{r \in \prod A_i} f\left(\lambda i. g(i, r_i)\right) $.

items.informal_name: Distributivity of Multilinear Maps over Finite Sums
items.type:
∀ {R : Type uR} {ι : Type uι} {M₁ : ι → Type v₁} {M₂ : Type v₂} [inst : Semiring R]
  [inst_1 : (i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (M₁ i)] [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid M₂] [inst_3 : (i : ι) → Module R (M₁ i)]
  [inst_4 : Module R M₂] (f : MultilinearMap R M₁ M₂) {α : ι → Type u_1} (g : (i : ι) → α i → M₁ i)
  [inst_5 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_6 : Fintype ι] [inst_7 : (i : ι) → Fintype (α i)],
  (f fun i => ∑ j, g i j) = ∑ r, f fun i => g i (r i)
items.informal_description: For a multilinear map $ f $ and a family of finite sums $ \sum_j g(i,j) $ in each component, applying $ f $ to the tuple of sums equals the sum over all possible combinations $ r $ of applying $ f $ to the tuple $ (g(i, r(i))) $, i.e., $$ f\left(\left(\sum_j g(i,j)\right)_{i}\right) = \sum_{r} f\left(\left(g(i, r(i))\right)_{i}\right), $$ where the sum on the right ranges over all functions $ r : \iota \to \bigcup_i \alpha(i) $ with $ r(i) \in \alpha(i) $.
